svg.title: kD, the damper: it brakes as the target gets close
svg.desc: Animated. Two blocks are driven from the left to the same dashed target line with the same kP. Top lane, P only: the block shoots past the target and swings back and forth. Bottom lane, P plus D: a blue arrow, the P push, points at the target and shrinks as the error shrinks; a green arrow, the D push, points the other way and grows with how fast the block is closing in, so as the target gets close it brakes the block and it stops on the target. Below, a graph of the bottom lane's pushes over time: the P line is big just after the start and fades, and the D line points opposite the P line as the target nears: that is braking.
svg.text: kD, the damper: it brakes as the target gets close
Push = kD × how fast the error changes, like a shock absorber.
P: big at the start, fades
D: opposite P as the target nears = braking
It lets you use more kP without overshoot.
Too much D amplifies sensor noise into buzzing, because noise changes quickly.
